question: Is the served static profile invariant to rule-preserving transformations: (a) 180-degree rotation of every movement atom on a square board, and (b) relabeling of piece type ids that keeps movement atoms, anchor flags and promotion edges isomorphic?
inputs: 40 deterministic generated rules already used in profile_normalization_scale_20261018 seeds 292001-292040 at board sizes 6 and 8, rebuilt with transformed movement atoms/type ids; zero search, zero new seeds; uses coordinates.rotate_offset for (a) and a pure renaming map for (b)
exclusions: no search, no learning, no fitness, no new rule family, no hand_weight sweep (PRIMARY target-sensitivity panel), no PRIMARY 411001-411008, no AUX92/93
endpoint: per-piece normalized_board_value, normalized_hand_value, promotion_option_value and median_non_anchor_value compared between original and transformed rule; violation = any per-piece value or per-rule median mismatch under a bijection that preserves the movement-signature multiset
pre_written_decision: 0 violations in both transforms on all 40 rules x 2 sizes => profile_transform_invariant; any violation whose pattern is explained by anchor/promotion/rounding mechanics and reproducible => transform_sensitive_with_mechanism; otherwise inconclusive
cost_estimate: under 5 min compute; under 60 min engineering total, well below the 120-minute assessment threshold
consumer: cross-rule static-value comparison and rule deduplication: a transform-equivalent rule must not be counted as an independent value sample, and any value dependence on labels/orientation would need an explicit interpretation boundary
feasibility_gate: first confirm that MovementAtom offsets accept rotate_offset and that a renamed ruleset compiles with identical fingerprints of movement; if either is unsupported, stop and record unsupported rather than fabricating a transform
nonduplication_check: read docs/research/RULE_ENCODING_NEUTRALITY_20261017.md and the PRIMARY 411001-411008 panel notes first; if profile-level equality under transforms is already covered, choose a different fallback question instead of rerunning
limitations: one generator family and hand_weight 0.9; rotation invariance is only defined on square boards; relabeling test cannot detect value dependence on type-id order because the builder sorts, which is itself the property under test at code level but not an independent behavioural sample
prior_work: PRIMARY RULE_ENCODING_NEUTRALITY_20261017 already shows a ray->leap syntactic re-encoding keeps raw score, normalized board/hand value and promotion option equal for 8 states in one rule; this plan does NOT re-test ray->leap. It tests two untested global transforms across 40 rules: 180-degree rotation of all movement atoms and type-id relabeling. If rotation invariance is not constructible from MovementAtom offsets without changing semantics, record unsupported and do not substitute a claimed transform.
